ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account action against either party.
ruling.reasoning:
The cancellation was made by the rider 1 min 40 s (100 s) after acceptance — 12:54:00 → 12:55:40 [F2] — so under NS-0 the rider-cancellation branch applies and the case is governed by NS-4, which makes all cancellations made within 3 minutes of matching not chargeable [F2][NS-0][NS-4]. The $6.61 on record [F5] therefore cannot stand on the rider-cancellation route.

The alternative route to the same charge — a rider no-show under NS-1 — also fails on the settled records: no arrival confirmation exists, the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival was recorded [F4][F3], so NS-1(i) is unmet; and the GPS record puts the driver's closest approach at 2138 m at 12:55:40, never within 200 m, so NS-1(ii) is unmet [F1][NS-1][NS-2]. With the rider cancelling 100 s after acceptance [F2] no continuous in-range wait could have accumulated, so NS-1(iii) fails as well [F2][F4][NS-1]. NS-2 consequently requires the rider's cancellation fee to be refunded in full [F1][F2][F4][F5][NS-2].

No waiting fee is in issue: none was charged, only the $6.61 cancellation fee appears on the record with a 1.0× multiplier and no surge component [F5][F6][NS-6]. The driver's post-trip statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" [F8] is a statement, not a chat message, and the system records [F1][F4] prevail over it; in any case it asserts no arrival and adds nothing [F8][F1][F4][NS-1]. There is no in-app chat at all [F7], so no contemporaneous rider-side conduct or agreement exists that could shift the fee.

The amount is the cancellation fee recorded as charged: $6.61 [F5], matching the timeline entry [F2]; no arithmetic beyond the recorded fee is needed because the trace fixes the full-fee refund under NS-4/NS-2 [F2][F5][NS-2][NS-4]. The profiles — rider with 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d [F12] and driver with a clean 90-day record [F13] — are background only and cannot decide the case or found a flag_account; no clause condition for flag_account (RD-6, NS-2 second limb) is met on this record [F12][F13][RD-6][NS-2].

rejected_claims.reason: Not rejected as to outcome but corrected as to route: the refund rests on NS-4 (cancellation within 3 minutes of matching, 100 s [F2]) and on NS-1/NS-2 failing, not on the no-show test alone [F2][NS-0][NS-4].
Accepted only insofar as the absence of chat [F7] leaves no rider-side conduct on record; the absence of chat is not itself proof and adds nothing beyond [F1][F3][F4][NS-2].

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (12:54:00 → 12:55:40), i.e. within the 3-minute window in which all cancellations are not chargeable, so the $6.61 cancellation fee should not stand.

No-show against the rider cannot be established because the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so requirement (i) of the no-show test fails.
The driver was never at the pickup point: his closest approach was 2138 m at 12:55:40 and he never came within 200 m, so requirement (ii) of NS-1 also fails and any waiting-based fee is unsupported.
Since (i) and (ii) of the no-show test are unmet, NS-2 requires the $6.61 rider cancellation fee to be refunded in full; the amount is the fee recorded at F5 and confirmed at F2.

The driver's written statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" (F8) concedes he had not arrived, and the system record of a 2138 m closest approach (F1) prevails over it; in any event NS-2 turns on the absence of an "I'm Here" tap and of GPS presence at the pickup, not on the driver's intentions.
No chat messages exist between the parties (F7), so there is no evidence of any rider-side no-show conduct or agreement that could shift the fee to the rider.

weaknesses: NS-4 confirms the rider's own cancellation was made after matching, so the fee was generated by the rider's cancel rather than by the driver cancelling; the charge is only defeated because no-show under NS-1/NS-2 is not made out — the judge may instead read NS-0 as routing a rider-cancellation case solely through NS-4 and find the $6.61 chargeable (F2, F5).

The rider's profile shows 2 no-show disputes upheld in the last 90 days (F12); the other side may use this pattern to suggest the rider habitually cancels, though F12 is a profile fact and cannot decide the case.

There is no record of why the rider cancelled at 12:55:40 beyond her own statement that the driver was "nowhere near"; F1 supports her on distance but the timeline gives no ETA field, and NS-8 (driver late beyond ETA → free cancellation) is informational only and cannot be cited.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee cannot stand as a rider no-show fee: the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and no arrival confirmation exists — the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival was recorded. Under NS-0 the only route to a $6.61 charge on a driver-side no-show theory is NS-1, which is not met.

The GPS record contradicts any arrival claim: the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 2138 m at 12:55:40 and he never came within 200 m, so NS-1 (ii) (driver within 200 m of the pickup when arriving) fails by a wide margin.

NS-1 (iii) also fails: there was no post-tap wait of more than 3 minutes, because the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (12:54:00 accepted, cancelled 12:55:40) and no arrival tap ever occurred, so no continuous in-range wait could have accumulated.

The charge cannot be justified on the rider side either: this was an instant booking and the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after matching, which is within the 3-minute window of NS-4 — cancellations made within 3 minutes of matching are not chargeable.

On the undisputed system record — no arrival, no approach within 200 m, cancellation inside 3 minutes — the only consistent outcome is that the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full (refund_full), the amount being the cancellation fee recorded as charged ($6.61).

weaknesses: The driver's own written statement (F8, "I was on my way when the rider cancelled") is consistent with him not having reached the pickup, and it does not assert any arrival or waiting; the rider will cite it as an admission that no pickup service was performed, which supports NS-2 against the driver.

The rider's 90-day profile shows two prior no-show disputes, both upheld against drivers (F12), which the rider may use to argue a pattern; this cuts the other way for us and is background only, not a finding.
There is no in-app chat at all (F7), so the driver has no contemporaneous record of any contact, route guidance, or notice to the rider to explain the 2138 m gap (F1).
The driver's otherwise clean record (F13, 1839 d, 4.76 rating, 0 upheld disputes in 90 days) does not cure the missing NS-1 elements and cannot be used to justify any charge.

points.response: Accepted and adopted: D1 matches my C2 — the platform recorded no arrival at the pickup (F3) and no "I'm Here" tap or automatic arrival (F4), so the driver-side no-show route in NS-1 is not made out and NS-2 applies.
Accepted and adopted: D2 matches my C3 — the driver's closest approach was 2138 m at 12:55:40 and he never entered the 200 m pickup radius (F1), so NS-1 (ii) fails.
Accepted: no continuous in-range wait could accumulate because the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (F2) and no arrival tap ever occurred (F4), so NS-1 (iii) fails as well.
Accepted and adopted: D4 is my C1 — this was an instant booking and the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after matching, i.e. within the 3-minute not-chargeable window of NS-4.

Accepted: on the undisputed record — no arrival (F4), no approach within 200 m (F1), cancellation inside 3 minutes (F2) — the $6.61 fee recorded as charged (F5, F6) must be refunded in full under NS-2 and NS-4; both advocates ask for the same relief, refund_full of $6.61.

Conceded as to the fee's validity, though not on their reasoning: NS-0 routes a rider-cancellation case through NS-4 only, and NS-4 makes a cancellation made 1 min 40 s after matching (12:54:00 → 12:55:40, F2) non-chargeable, so the $6.61 on record (F5) cannot stand either way.
Accepted: F4 records driver_pressed_here_at as null with no automatic arrival, so NS-1 (i) is unmet and my brief already relies on that record (D1) rather than disputing it.

Accepted: F1 puts the driver's closest approach at 2138 m at 12:55:40 and never within 200 m, and F3 records no arrival, so NS-1 (ii) fails; no waiting-fee question arises because no $5.00 waiting fee was charged (F5, F6).

Agreed in substance: on this record nothing supports the $6.61, and NS-2 requires full refund of the rider cancellation fee, the amount being the $6.61 recorded as charged at F5 with no surge component (F6, multiplier 1.0×).
Undisputed: F8 is a post-trip statement, not a chat message, and the system records (F1, F4) prevail over it; it does not assert any arrival, so it adds nothing either way.

Undisputed: F7 records no in-app chat, so there is no rider-side conduct or agreement on record; note that the absence of chat does not itself prove anything beyond what F1/F3/F4 already establish, and no flag_account is sought against the driver on this record (F13 shows 0 upheld disputes in 90 d).

notices.text: You cancelled 1 minute 40 seconds after a driver was matched, so the cancellation fee doesn't apply and we've refunded it in full. The $6.61 fee is coming back to you as a Ryde voucher — same value, no cash-out needed, it'll show in your vouchers once issued. The deciding facts: you cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, and the driver never confirmed arriving at your pickup point and was recorded well over 200 m away, so no no-show charge could apply either. No action is being taken on your account.

The rider cancelled 1 minute 40 seconds after you were matched, which is inside the 3-minute window, so the $6.61 cancellation fee can't be charged and is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. Records show no arrival was confirmed for this trip — no "I'm Here" tap and no automatic arrival — and your closest recorded position was a long way from the pickup point, so a no-show fee couldn't stand either. This doesn't affect your account: no penalty, no flag, no change to your standing. Payouts are unaffected.
